text: David Jones. Hi, stabbing a man in the back, sir.
You had us all at your mercy.
There was no need for you to kill, Cooper.
I fancied better odds than five against one, Sawbones.
What is it you want of us?
By the secret force, wherever his goal lies.
And suppose we refuse to tell you?
Do you fancy these lads of yours meeting their maker so young, eh, Sawbones?
I'm not going to bargain with you, sir. Where is your captain?
Oh, you fancy you'd twist him out of your way, would you?
Listen. Not here, matey. There's only one skipper here, mate.
That's right, matey, but I'm no fool, so...
One false move and I'll split you in two.
Leave this to me, Ben, my boy.
That's right. Let the old fella do the talking, cos he knows the answers.
But what about the squire? He's badly wounded. He needs help.
Now, Sawbones, talk, or the young lad dies.
We must play for time now. Trust me.
Well, I must admit the church warden did tell me something,
but to be quite honest with you, I am dothoed.
A ringwood, a small beer, and gurney.
No, no, I know those names.
Old Jack Ringwood, he had a wooden leg.
He was the finest master gunner that never served his king.
A fella that sold money immersion into a sailcloth mic gown.
A sailor's shroud of you, boy.
And Daniel Smallbeard, there was a man.
Pointed up inside of him, and he was like a killer whale.
Tim Deadman, he was Avery's galley boy.
Now, what else did he tell you?
I said I needed your help.
And that's all he told you?
Avery's curse, you can have that for the sharks.
Did he not die a pauper?
Aye, rotten with rum and madness in his tongue.
They say he bargained for his life.
His soul in return for the souls of those
who come after seeking and finding the cursed treasure.
And if you so believe it,
why did you seek the gold, eh, Sir Squire?
Because I was a fool and ill-led.
You know more than I will hear it said.
Tell me now what the riddle means,
Find Cherub for me, wherever he is.
Captain, is it to be carried back straight away?
Set the goods upon the shore.
Do as ye bid, ye dog,
or I'll leave ye in the coffin as a souvenir.
If your tongue's up, Sawbone, so spake.
What would ye have him say, Cherub boy?
I knew there was some trickery for him.
Didn't I say so? Tell me again.
I never did trust that tongue of yours, Cherub,
to the mite too like the archangel's.
But I found the Sawbone, didn't I?
Aye, ye did find the gold, too, eh?
But I was making him talk, Captain, see?
He spoke of oldie Joe's riddle.
He was gonna spill the old cargo.
I wasn't gonna let no one do you down, Captain.
Well, he'd have napped it all for himself, see?
He'd have done for his bone.
So that's a game, eh, Sawbones?
No, the doctor wouldn't take no one.
He met the doom now, my Cherub.
Not from such a black pig as ye.
Only watch the hook, boy, for when it whistles,
Spills rats, get on with it.
And you, Spaniard, do as you're bitten.
Pike finds you idle in here, you'll lose your ears
But you, Spaniard, and you, David, to the beach with you.
Get Polly back to the TARDIS, and I will follow immediately
But I can't leave you here alone.
There is no other way, child.
Without either of you, they can't hold a hostage for me
But suppose I start on you.
Oh, I've done it before, my dear boy.
I somehow don't think that Master Cherub will be the winner.
If you're not back by then, I'm coming for you.
Well, now, Cherub, you'll not need prayers in this company, eh?
Now, old man, the time has come.
I think we agreed on that point previously.
My dear captain, I had every intention of telling you.
And that's why you fled the ship?
Where are they, stowed away sawbones?
Is there another passage out of the script?
Aye, I'll live to see you hanged.
I made a bargain with you, sir.
Don't you want me to keep it?
Aye, that sounds like the foolishness of an honest man.
I wish to keep my side of the bargain.
But I want to change the terms of my plans.
I prefer to call them humane, sir.
And ye'd want none of the gold?
I would rather not touch it.
I have given you all my reasons.
I want no part of the gold.
Though perhaps I can deliver it to you immediately.
If I keep my lads out of the village?
There is no need for innocent people to suffer.
I like my lads to be happy, Sawbones.
You'd have Avery's gold at our stores, would you, villain?
We have an uneasy conscience, have we, squire?
Ye dare to call me villain?
Though I've been a rogue, I frankly admit it.
But the generosity of this stranger has shamed me.
But I'd never spill blood in my villainy.
I beg you, as a fellow rogue, if you must, spare my poor village, sir.
When the fever is in the lads' bones, sir, I'll do it.
Nothing but blood will slake it.
It is my way of being a pastime with us gentlemen of fortune.
Told. You admit it to be difficult, eh?
You'd rather let them run mad than test their obedience, eh, captain?
No man defies me and lives to speak of it.
No, but you do not give that one order, eh?
A highly disciplined crew, in truth.
They'll do as I bid or die of it.
I suppose we must trust you.
And take heed of cherub yonder, eh, sawbones?
I am not delighted to try and cheat you just as he did.
Come on, Ducks. We're nearly there.
I told you, we're nearly there. It's only about another hundred yards.
Well, look, you go back and get the doctor, then.
Well, will you be all right?
Look, hurry, I'll see you back at the Tardis.
All right, I've nothing to do. The rest of you, come with me.
The church warden set me a riddle which involved four names.
Ringwood, Small Bear, Gurney, and Deadman,
which should be on that wall's end.
Four names of Avery's crew in the old days.
They died on the seven seas, all of them.
The original names were changed by the church warden.
And unless I am very much mistaken, sir,
this flagstone is at the intersection of those fateful names.
Aye, and it's loose. Stand aside.
I think that is what you seek.
What price, you damned Avery, now?
I swear you'll lie beneath that!
And for that, you'll die by the pipe!
Oh, I must try and help the squire.
I'll try and get you out of here.
That is quite surrender, I say!
I think we've managed very well, you and I.
I will offer my gratitude to him.
A little exhausted, my dear, otherwise I'm all right.
I thought the doctor nearly had it when old Pike got going.
What happened? How did you all escape?
So they're all dead, then, the ones who wanted the treasure?
Yes, superstition is a strange thing, my dear.
But sometimes it tells the truth.
Now, doctor, will we go forward or back in time?
I have no control over such matter.
Well, it better be 1966 or I'm in dead trouble, doctor.
Anyway, wherever he is, it can't be as bad as going back to them days.
My dear boy, it could be a great deal worse.
It's getting right parky in here.
Just look up at that scanner.
We have arrived at the coldest place in the world.
